source.title: Jedno ti nedostaje: EP 65 - Večera je spremna - fra Ante Vučković i Stanko Stojić

summary.title_hr: Jedno ti nedostaje: EP 65 - Večera je spremna - fra Ante Vučković i Stanko Stojić
summary.abstract_hr: U 65. epizodi emisije Jedno ti nedostaje voditelj Stanko Stojić i fra Ante Vučković tumače odlomak iz 14. poglavlja Markova evanđelja o pripremi pashalne večere i najavi izdaje. Fra Ante objašnjava židovski kontekst Pashe i Isusovo proročko znanje koje se očituje u uputama učenicima. Ističe da Isus svjesno i suvereno prihvaća put koji ga čeka, a odbacuje new age tumačenje čovjeka s krčagom vode kao najave doba vodenjaka. Sugovornici se osvrću i na otuđenost suvremenog čovjeka od izvora hrane, na biblijske korijene hrvatskog jezika te na pitanje Judine slobode i konačne sudbine. Emisija završava porukom da treba sada naći vremena za bliske odnose, a ne čekati neko bolje vrijeme.
key_points: Fra Ante objašnjava da je priprema Pashe uključivala osiguravanje prostora, obredno klanje janjeta u hramu, pripremu gorkog zelja i vina. Marko te detalje pretpostavlja i ne opisuje ih jer su bili dio svakodnevnog života.
Isusove upute o čovjeku s krčagom vode nisu dogovoreno namještanje, nego izraz njegova znanja o svemu što ga čeka. Isus taj put prihvaća svjesno i suvereno, bez stvaranja emotivne drame.
Tumačenje čovjeka s krčagom vode kao najave 'doba vodenjaka' fra Ante smatra proizvoljnim i neutemeljenim. Za Marka novo doba dolazi s Kristom i njegovim uskrsnućem.
Marko ne imenuje izdajnika, a učenici pitaju 'Da nisam ja?'. Prema fra Anti, time se čitatelja poziva da preispita vlastiti odnos s Učiteljem, a ne da traži tko je izdajnik.
Izdaja onoga koji s nekim dijeli stol, slika preuzeta iz Psalma 41, najdublja je rana jer dolazi iz blizine. Hrvatski jezik prožet je biblijskim slikama i metaforama.
Bog upravlja poviješću, ali to ne umanjuje Judinu slobodu i odgovornost. Juda nije bio predodređen za izdaju, a njegova konačna sudbina ostaje skrivena Bogu.
Budući da malo tko zna kad će otići iz ovoga života, treba već sada naći vremena, pozornosti i prostora za bliske odnose.
key_topics_en: betrayal and the question 'Is it I?'
the Bible and the Croatian language
key_points_en: Fra Ante explains that the preparation of Passover involved securing space, the ritual slaughter of the lamb in the Temple, and preparing bitter herbs and wine. Mark assumes these details and does not describe them because they were part of everyday life.

Jesus' instructions regarding the man with the pitcher of water are not an agreed-upon setup, but an expression of His knowledge of everything that awaits Him. Jesus accepts that path consciously and sovereignly, without creating emotional drama.

Fra Ante considers the interpretation of the man with the pitcher of water as an announcement of the 'Age of Aquarius' arbitrary and unfounded. For Mark, the new age comes with Christ and His resurrection.

Mark does not name the betrayer, and the disciples ask 'Is it I?'. According to fra Ante, this invites the reader to examine their own relationship with the Teacher, rather than search for who the betrayer is.

The betrayal of one who shares a table with someone, an image taken from Psalm 41, is the deepest wound because it comes from proximity. The Croatian language is permeated with biblical images and metaphors.
God directs history, but that does not diminish Judas' freedom and responsibility. Judas was not predestined to betray, and his final destiny remains hidden with God.
Since few know when they will depart from this life, one should already now find time, attention, and space for close relationships.
summary.title_en: One Thing You Lack: EP 65 - Supper Is Ready - fra Ante Vučković and Stanko Stojić
summary.abstract_en: In the 65th episode of the show One Thing You Lack, host Stanko Stojić and fra Ante Vučković interpret a passage from the 14th chapter of Mark's Gospel on the preparation of the Passover meal and the announcement of the betrayal. Fra Ante explains the Jewish context of Passover and Jesus' prophetic knowledge manifested in the instructions to the disciples. He emphasizes that Jesus consciously and sovereignly accepts the path awaiting Him, and rejects the New Age interpretation of the man with the pitcher of water as an announcement of the Age of Aquarius. The interlocutors also reflect on the alienation of modern man from food sources, on the biblical roots of the Croatian language, and on the question of Judas' freedom and ultimate destiny. The show concludes with the message that one should find time for close relationships now, rather than waiting for some better time.
